blocks.text:
I need to identify which chain B residues have heavy atoms within 4.0 Å of chain A atoms, given chain A spans residues 3-152 and chain B spans 341-361. I'll work through this systematically, checking each chain B residue's coordinates against nearby chain A atoms, starting with K341.

Most of these chain A residues are too far away in x-coordinate to be relevant, but residues 25-30 (SER25 through GLU30) fall in a plausible range worth checking more closely.

I'm checking the distance between chain B Y342 and chain A's GLU30 region, but it comes out too far at ~8.6Å, so that's not the interface. I'm now scanning chain A residues in the y~-5 to -13, z~0-13 range to see if they align better with chain B's 350-361 segment.

Looking at PHE41's ring atoms against chain B V354, the z-distance is still too large. Checking A357, R358, K359, G360, Y361 against chain A's PRO20-GLY23 stretch, VAL22 and GLY23 come closest but still roughly 6Å off from G360/Y361. I'm starting to think the real interface might involve chain A's 56-66 region instead, so I need to pull those coordinates and compare systematically.

Checking chain B's lower-z residues like A357, R358, G360, Y361 against chain A candidates, but the distances still seem too large. Looking back at chain A's GLY23/VAL24/SER25 region to see if those residues might actually form the contact interface instead.

I compute SER25's OG to A357's CB as 3.79 Å, which confirms a real interface contact between A:S25 and B:A357. Now I need to set up a systematic bounding box approach, estimating chain B's coordinate ranges so I can filter chain A atoms before computing all pairwise distances.

Since scanning the full chain A atom list is unwieldy, I decide to go residue-by-residue through chain B, checking each CA against nearby chain A atoms within roughly 8 Å. I'm compiling the CA coordinates for chain B residues K341 through Q351 to use as reference points for this proximity search.

Continuing to scan, I don't find chain A atoms near the expected region for K341-K345, so those residues may lack close contacts. I'm now checking whether R343 or H346 have any nearby chain A atoms, but nothing in that coordinate range turns up so far.

Checking E349, though, I find a strong candidate: its OE1 atom sits just 2.91 Å from ASN37's ND2 on chain A, a distance consistent with a hydrogen bond, confirming A:N37 contacts B:E349. This tells me the actual interface centers around chain A residues roughly 29-39, so I need to systematically gather all chain A atoms in that spatial region to map contacts against the chain B stretch from E349 through Y361.

Going through residues 3-9 on chain A one by one, I'm checking their side chain atom coordinates against the box boundaries, but most residues 3-8 fall outside the x/y/z ranges. Residue 9 (Leu) has some atoms borderline in range, but comparing against chain B coordinates shows no chain B atoms at matching y-values, so I'm ruling that out and narrowing the interface to chain B residues with y roughly between -1 and -17.

Now I'm pulling the chain A CA coordinates for residues 20 through 41, planning to measure distances from each to chain B CA positions to find residues within contact range of the interface.

Continuing to scan, I'm noting chain A residues in the 70-90 and 50-55 ranges with positive x/z values as possible interface candidates, while comparing them against chain B's low-z residues (357-361) which sit in a negative-x region far from chain A's positive-x cluster—suggesting those aren't likely contacts. I'm narrowing in on chain A's 22-42 stretch plus possibly 52-54 as the real interface, checking specific pairs like THR52 against chain B's V354 to see if their CA-CA distance (~6.9 Å) is close enough for side-chain contact.

Working through the atom-by-atom distances, I find THR52 and V354 don't quite make contact (closest atoms are ~4.75 Å apart, just outside the 4 Å threshold), so I rule that pair out. But checking PHE41 against ARG358 reveals a genuine contact—their side-chain atoms come within about 3.75 Å of each other, confirming an interface between chain A's F41 and chain B's R358.

Now I'm systematically scanning chain A for any atoms with larger x-coordinates and z-coordinates that could reach chain B residues 341-348, checking residues 42 through 54 one by one, noting coordinates for prolines, phenylalanines, aspartate, glycine, threonine, and lysine side chains to see which might fall within contact range of that chain B segment.

I find the highest reaching chain A atom there is LYS54's CE around z 8.7, which still falls short of chain B's K341-K347 cluster sitting around x 4-16, z 1-18. I'm now cross-checking chain B's Y342 aromatic ring coordinates against this to confirm whether any real contact exists.

Measuring distances, I find GLN35's side chain atoms (CD, NE2) actually sit close enough to Y342's OH and ring carbons to register as a contact, within the 4.0 Å cutoff — so the A:Q35/B:Y342 interface is real after all. This tells me the true interface is larger than I initially assumed, so I need a more systematic approach: build a filtered list of chain A atoms within a bounding region to check against chain B systematically rather than spot-checking pairs.

I'm cataloguing chain A's CA coordinates for residues 3 through 24 that fall within the relevant z-range, so I can narrow down which chain A residues are actually positioned near the chain B interface before computing pairwise distances.

Chain B sits further out in z with mostly negative y, so I'm checking which chain A residues (22-42, 52-56, 73-74, 25-29, 35-37) could be close enough to contact it. Going through residue K341 and Y342 coordinates, I see K341 is too far from any chain A atom given the x-range mismatch, but Y342's position puts it near GLN35 on chain A, so I'm comparing their side-chain coordinates to check for a possible contact.

Measuring distances from Y342's hydroxyl oxygen to nearby chain A atoms, I find it's close enough to GLN35's amide nitrogen for a contact, and also near ASN37's side-chain oxygen and nitrogen, plus SER29's hydroxyl group — several plausible hydrogen-bonding contacts clustering around this region.

I'm now shifting to B chain ARG343's extended side chain, checking its guanidinium and aliphatic atoms against nearby A chain residues like LEU73 and SER74, but the distances I'm finding for LEU73's branches are just slightly over typical contact thresholds.

Confirming precisely: CB73 to R343 CG gives 3.97, under 4.0, so B:R343 does contact A:L73. I'm double-checking the coordinates against the PDB records to be sure, and now checking R343 CD against LEU73 CB for another potential close contact.

Moving on to scan the rest of chain B's K344 and K345 residues against chain A, checking their backbone and sidechain atoms against the chain A residues within range -- K344 looks too far given its z-coordinates relative to chain A, while K345 needs checking against GLU30 given their similar z-range.

After confirming the close distance between K345's NZ and GLU30's OE2 (about 3.85 Å, well within contact range), I conclude that K345 forms a contact with A:E30. Then I move to checking H346's atoms against chain A's SER29, comparing their coordinates to see if the distance falls within contact threshold.

Working through H346's CD2 and NE2 distances to S29 and OE2 of E30, I find contacts at roughly 3.2-3.3 Å, confirming H346 interacts with both A:S29 and A:E30. I verify the ND1 position doesn't yield any close chain A neighbors, then move on to analyzing K347's backbone atom coordinates for its potential contacts.

Checking chain A's spatial distribution, I don't find any residues positioned near K347's y/z coordinates—the closest chain A atoms are too far given the negative y and high z range, so K347 appears to have no contacts.

I run the same check for S348, scanning through chain A's residue clusters by z-range, and again find nothing close enough in the relevant y/z window, so S348 also has no contacts. I'm now starting the backbone coordinate analysis for E349.

For E349 I calculate distances to nearby chain A atoms and find a match with ASN37's ND2 to the glutamate's OE1, plus a contact with SER29's OG via both the CD and OE1 positions — confirming E349 bridges to A:S29 and A:N37. Moving on, I'm pulling the backbone and side-chain coordinates for F350 to begin its contact analysis.

Checking F350's phenyl ring atoms against ASN37, I'm testing distances between its CD2/CG and N37's CG/CB, getting values near 4.8-5.0 — close but not quite within contact range, so I pivot to checking LYS54's side chain instead, comparing F350's CE1, CZ, and CE2 atoms to K54's CD position, again landing around 4.5-5.0 without a clear hit. I'm now pulling LEU55's coordinates to continue the search.

Checking CZ against N37 OD1 gives 3.77, confirming a contact, so F350 touches both A:N37 and A:K54 but nothing else nearby. Now I'm moving on to B:Q351, laying out its backbone and side-chain atom coordinates to begin distance checks against chain A.

Scanning for chain A atoms near Q351's y/z range, I find nothing close enough, so Q351 has no contacts. Then I do the same for B:L352, listing its coordinates and checking against chain A positions, again finding no residues within range, so L352 has no contacts either. I'm now double-checking by scanning chain A more broadly for atoms with y between -9 and -4 and z between 10 and 18, looking specifically at residue 110 to confirm nothing was missed.

Confirming chain A's GLN110 stays at negative z, so no contacts with L352. Now checking chain B's L353 coordinates against nearby chain A residues like SER25, ALA38, and ASN37, measuring distances to see if any fall within contact range.

I'm finding that L353's CD1 atom is close enough to several A38 and A37 atoms—N37's backbone C, CA, CB, and O—to count as contacts, with distances around 3.6-4.3 Å. Now I'm moving on to checking CD2's distances to the same nearby residues.

Working through L353's CD2 against A26's CA, N, and C atoms, plus A25's OG, I'm confirming these all fall within contact range (roughly 3.7-3.8 Å). I also check CG and CB against S25's OG, finding CB qualifies at 3.48 Å while CG is slightly too far at 4.17 Å—so overall L353 makes contacts with S25, G26, and N37.

I check A27's CB and CA against L353's CD2 and CG, but both distances exceed 4 Å, so no contact there. The backbone oxygen of L353 comes very close to S25's OG at 2.67 Å, confirming that contact again. Moving on, I start setting up coordinates for V354 to check its proximity to chain A residues near VAL39.

For V354, I scan nearby chain A atoms around VAL39, ILE40, PHE41, and THR52, but most distances land in the 4.4-5.5 Å range, so they're probably not contacts. Then I find that S25's OG comes to 3.97 Å from V354's backbone nitrogen, just barely under the 4 Å cutoff, giving another borderline contact with A:S25.

Wait, I realize I mixed up coordinates — I need to double-check the actual N position for VAL B 354 since I may have pulled the wrong atom's value, which would throw off this distance calculation.

Confirming V354 N coordinates, then checking the distance from S25 OG to V354 N — too far at 4.53 Å, not a contact. I continue scanning nearby atoms like VAL39's CG1 and CG2 for possible proximity to V354 CG2, but these also look too distant.

Rechecking V354 CG2 against VAL39 CG2 more precisely, I get a distance of 3.975 Å, which just barely falls within the 4.0 Å contact threshold — confirming V354 contacts A:V39. I verify both atom coordinates against the source file to make sure this borderline result is accurate, then check a few more nearby pairs (V354 CB to V39 CG2, V354 CG2 to V39 CB, and others) to see if additional contacts exist, but none come in under 4.0 Å.

Moving on, I check ASP355 and GLN356 from chain B against nearby chain A residues like PHE41, but the coordinates show these are too far apart (5+ Å in the z-direction) to register as contacts. I'm now checking GLN356's atoms against chain A residues in a similar coordinate range to look for any additional interactions.

Testing SER25's CB and OG atoms against Q356's CB position gives distances around 3.9-4.3 Å, close enough to flag as a contact, so I'm recording Q356 as interacting with A:S25. I rule out other nearby chain A residues like VAL24, PRO20, and GLY23 since their z-coordinates are too far off.

Now I'm pulling the backbone and CB coordinates for chain B's ALA357 to begin checking its proximity to chain A residues next.

Checking G23's atoms too: A357 CB to G23 C comes out to 3.93, confirming contact. The O atom also falls within range at 3.89, and I'm continuing to check CA against G23 O.

So A357 contacts A:G23 and A:S25 confirmed. Now checking V24 systematically against all A357 atoms - closest pairs hover right around the 4.0 cutoff, with V24-C to A357-CB landing at exactly 4.008, just barely exceeding the threshold, so I'll exclude V24. Moving on to check B R358 next.

Listing R358's atom coordinates (N, CA, C, O, CB, CG, CD, NE, CZ, NH1, NH2) and comparing against chain A's PHE41, whose atoms I'm also laying out. Measuring the distance from R358's CA to F41's CZ gives roughly 3.75, a solid contact, and I'm now computing R358's N to F41's CZ distance as well.

Checking CB to CZ confirms another close contact around 3.78, so R358 is clearly interacting with A:F41. I scan other nearby chain A residues (GLY42, GLU44, THR52, ASP50, GLY51) but none come close enough to count as contacts, so R358's interaction is isolated to F41. Moving on to B:K359, I start listing its backbone and side chain coordinates (N, CA, C, O, CB, CG) to begin the same contact analysis.

Checking chain A residues near Y361's ring atoms, PHE41, GLY42, and PRO43 all fall within plausible contact range based on their coordinates.

I'm computing distances between Y361's hydroxyl ring atoms (CD1, CE1, CZ, OH, CE2) and nearby chain A residues like PHE41 and GLY42, finding several under the ~4Å contact threshold — notably Y361 CZ/OH to GLY42's backbone oxygen looks like a solid hydrogen-bonding contact around 2.6-3.3Å.

I also found a new contact: Y361 CD2 to PHE41 CD2 comes out to about 3.94Å, confirming another interaction with F41, while checking a few more atom pairs (CE2-CE2, CG-CD2) that fall just outside the cutoff.

Then I realize I'm overcomplicating things - since the question only asks which chain B residues contact chain A, I don't need to track which specific chain A residue each contact is with. I just need a yes/no per chain B residue, so I'm compiling that running tally: 341 no, 342 yes, 343 yes (borderline), 344 no, 345 yes, 346 yes, and continuing through the remaining residues.

Continuing the list: 347 no, 348 no, 349 yes, 350 yes, 351 no, 352 no, 353 yes, 354 yes (borderline), 355 no, 356 yes, 357 yes, 358 yes, 359 no, 360 no, 361 yes. Now I want to double-check the "no" calls, especially 344, 347, 348, 351, 352, 355, 359, 360, so I'm re-scanning chain A for residues with high z-coordinates and cross-referencing their x-coordinates to confirm K344 and similar residues are indeed too far from any chain A atom to count as contacts.

Moving to K347 and S348, I'm comparing their coordinates against nearby chain A residues like SER29, GLU30, and ASN31, finding the y-coordinate gaps are too large (around 10 units) to count as contacts, confirming both as no. For Q351, I'm now checking chain A atoms in the matching z-range with negative y-coordinates to see if any fall close enough.
